admission.justification: OR-R009 released the tree's coverage and presence fields and the shared renderer's opt-in extension and removed the private copies; those constraints govern every later coverage and renderer change on this page. No claim of weighed design alternatives is made.

alternatives.option: Release the bounded design: directory-only coverage, hasOverview and hasKnowledge on the existing tree route from one selected-memory settings read, one code subtree pathname pass and one memory pathname enumeration with linear immediate-child aggregation, and opt-in text-only markers and heading IDs on the shared Markdown renderer.
alternatives.reason: The ruling's own release states exactly these fields, these reads and this aggregation; it preserves onboarding and adds no records field.

alternatives.option: Record the design rationale as onboarding prose and demote this decision record.
alternatives.reason: The memory review's sealed finding L79-MR1-21 found no durable evidence that the private-renderer or contents/hash routes were weighed as live design choices and offered prose demotion instead; OR-R009 is a durable Orchestrator ruling that still constrains every later coverage and renderer change, so the record is kept.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The ruling's constraints are superseded, or another record carries them.

consequences: The tree route gained directory-only coverage and presence fields; a failure is a named unavailable count, not a zero.
The shared renderer's new plugins are opt-in, so every other consumer renders as before.
The private renderer, code view and tree of the old page are removed.
context: MIK-R79@v1 left two truth gaps to be read from the code before building: whether the route already carries a directory's coverage counts, and whether the shared Markdown renderer can draw `[n]` markers and resolve links between cards. Orchestrator ruling OR-R009 (2026-10-06T10:23:26, 'OR-R009 supplements OR-R008 and releases the bounded L79 backend/shared-renderer design') resolved both within the packet's promise.
decider: Orchestrator 71d18fce-4cb8-4a37-8dff-563bf4962b96, ruling OR-R009 (2026-10-06), on MIK-R79@v1; the packet's architect approval does not transfer this design authority.
